The recA protein is a multifunctional protein.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and functions of the DNA helix.
the study of the mechanism of DNA replication.
the study of the structure and function of DNA and DNA-protein interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA helix is a flexible structure that may be unwound by a variety of proteins and enzymes.
we have a good knowledge about the structure, function and regulation of DNA topoisomerases.

DNA topoisomerases are involved in all processes of DNA metabolism and in all stages of the cell cycle, and that they are required for DNA synthesis in vivo and in vitro, for the initiation of replication, for the elongation of DNA, for the termination of replication, for repair, for transcription and translation, for the segregation of chromosomes and for recombination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the DNA helical structure is controlled by proteins, and that the proteins are able to bind DNA with high specificity and with a very high binding affinity.
we have shown that the recA protein is an important factor in the regulation of the SOS response.
DNA topoisomerases of both type I and II are involved in DNA recombination.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the DNA-binding proteins that we studied, the SSB proteins, can be divided into two groups: the first group is the SSB proteins that bind DNA in a sequence-specific manner and are able to form stable complexes with DNA; the second group is the SBB proteins that bind DNA nonspecifically and are not able to form stable DNA complexes.
the DNA helix is a dynamic structure, which can be altered in a number of ways.
DNA topoisomerases are not just passive machines that passively change the topology of DNA.
